content.text: Nikola Jokic and the Denver Nuggets host rookie Cooper Flagg and the Dallas Mavericks for the first time this season. Heading into Cooper Flagg’s first game against the Denver Nuggets (14-5), the rookie is coming off the best game of his career. Flagg led the Dallas Mavericks (6-15) to the team’s second win in seven games. He finished with 35 points and eight rebounds on 13-22 shooting. Dallas is now in a position to win back-to-back games for the first time this season. Three-time MVP Nikola Jokic is looking to get Denver back on track at home after winning its first six games in Ball Arena. Since then, Denver has lost three straight at home, a rarity in the Jokic era. This season, Flagg has been the catalyst for Dallas in wins. He is averaging 22.3 points, 7.3 rebounds, and 4.3 assists per game on 55.7% shooting in wins. When Flagg plays well, Dallas plays well this season. For Denver, the defense has slipped dramatically over the last three home games. They have allowed 132.3 points per game in losses to the Chicago Bulls, Sacramento Kings, and San Antonio Spurs. One bright spot for Denver in recent weeks has been the play of Peyton Watson. He has filled in for the injured Aaron Gordon and Christian Braun, averaging 15.8 points per game on 47.1% shooting from three as a starter.
